probe.note: Probe loads the DEFAULT camera, which attempt 1 reframed onto the hero band, so most of the plan is frustum-culled and the probe under-reads. It is a floor, not a representative load. The writer's scene-graph analysis reports 115 draw buckets. Budget is a ceiling, so this passes; the representative figure is re-measured at the optimization pass.

root_cause_of_attempt2_failure: Attempt 2's derived tests composed the pixel as albedo * irradiance with NO RECIPROCAL_PI. three.js r160 runs useLegacyLights=false, so every reflected term passes through BRDF_Lambert = RECIPROCAL_PI * diffuseColor. The renderer was 3.14x darker than the test model for LIT surfaces only — emissives carry no PI, which is exactly why strips, screens and exit signs looked right while everything around them rendered black. Attempt 2's own rig through the correct chain: corridor 0.125, auditorium 0.032. Compounding it, ACES has a subtractive toe that crushes anything under ~0.002 linear to literal zero. Separately, corridorHalfWidth was 3.6 while the corridor walls, portal headers and door leaves stand at x = +/-3.72 — every surface the corridor camera looks at was being lit as auditorium, six stops down.

zone_luminance_multisurface.method: sRGB luminance, lights ON, sampled on MULTIPLE surfaces per zone including ones NOT under a fixture (the sampling error that made attempt 2's green tests meaningless)
